keyVerseText: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
rootMeaning: The word ἀπαύγασμα (apaúgasma) is derived from a compound of ἀπό (apó), meaning "off" or "away from," and αὐγάζω, meaning "to radiate or reflect." This etymology conveys the idea of light that beams or shines outward from a source, emphasizing not just brightness but the emanation or effulgence that comes from a luminous body. Thus, the root sense highlights a dynamic radiance that is an extension or reflection of an original brightness, rather than a static glow.
usageInScripture: This term appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Hebrews 1:3, where it is translated as "the brightness." Its singular occurrence and consistent translation as brightness or effulgence suggest a focused theological use, emphasizing the radiant glory that emanates from God. The word captures the visible manifestation of divine glory, revealing the nature of Christ as the luminous reflection of God’s glory.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἀπαύγασμα as the radiance or effulgence of divine glory enriches our grasp of Christ’s identity and work. It portrays Jesus not merely as a reflection but as the very brightness that beams forth from God the Father, signifying His divine nature and unity with the Father. This radiance also underscores Christ’s role in sustaining all creation by His powerful word, revealing Him as the visible expression of the invisible God. For believers, this word encourages faith in Christ’s divine authority and the transformative power of His glory shining into our lives.
keyVerseReflection: Hebrews 1:3 describes Christ as "the brightness of his glory," using ἀπαύγασμα to express how Jesus radiates the Father’s glory in an active, luminous way. This word captures the profound truth that Christ is the exact and visible representation of God’s nature, not a mere image but the effulgent expression of divine majesty. It highlights His unique position at God’s right hand and His sustaining power over all things, affirming His supremacy and the fullness of His divine person.
